evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2026-10-01"} returned 201 with dueDate "2026-10-01". POST without dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null. The date is a plain calendar date, and a datetime string was rejected with 400.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/2 with {"dueDate":"2026-09-30"} returned 200 and the new date. PATCH /todos/1 with {"dueDate":null} returned 200 with dueDate null, so the date was removed.
evidence.AC3: On POST, dueDate "2026-02-30", "10/01/2026" and "2026-10-01T10:00:00Z" each returned 400 with the error 'dueDate must be a valid date in YYYY-MM-DD format or null'. PATCH with "2026-02-30" also returned 400.
evidence.AC4: Today in UTC is 2026-10-14. GET /todos?overdue=true returned only the not-done todo due 2026-09-30. It excluded the todo due today (2026-10-14), the todo with no due date, a todo due 2026-12-01, and the done todo due 2026-09-01. That done todo showed overdue:true before PATCH {"done":true} and overdue:false after.
evidence.AC5: The page at / showed a <time> element with the due date for each todo that has one: 2026-09-30, 2026-10-14 and 2026-09-01. Todos without a date showed none.
evidence.AC6: In the page snapshot, only the overdue todo 'future' (due 2026-09-30) had the text 'überfällig'. The todos due today, with no date, and done with a past date had no such marker.
evidence.AC7: The page has a checkbox labelled 'nur überfällige'. After I clicked it, the list showed only the 'future' todo (due 2026-09-30, marked überfällig). The other four todos were no longer listed.
